scope: Independent visual review preparation for a newly redrawn clothing01 front/back collar pair; not an approval or an implementation.
rejected_method: The gap-only candidate replaced thin collar peaks with thick rounded rolled fabric and created mechanically vertical cloth/neck contact. Alpha40 gap0 and old single-layer guard passes do not establish a natural collar.
selection_rule: Both clothing textures belong to one existing clothing index; no independently selected back-collar option.

face_support_from_frozen_face.interpretation: The upper side contacts can belong to the rear collar and be naturally occluded by the neck. The y580 skin points are hidden support, not targets that force the front V to follow skin.

visible_review: Inspect upper neck and thin collar peaks without hair on both pale and dark backgrounds, then inspect with the actual first front/back hair.
Rear collar keeps continuous cloth underneath the neck; its center must not appear across the skin in the final composition.
Original thin outer peak height, outer frame and fabric thickness stay recognizably close to the original garment; do not inflate them into a rolled collar just to touch the neck.
Front collar blends into its original V from approximately y550 downward, preserving the measured y580/600/620 front V and the frozen body below y620.
The rear-to-front transition should read as one folded garment: continuous brocade, clean stitch/trim line, no doubled trim, exposed rectangular cut or sharp vertical painted stripe.
Coverage is tested on the composed rear+face+front, not by requiring the front texture alone to hug every neck contour row.
No visible background slit or bright alpha fringe remains between skin and collar, but absence of gaps remains only one condition among shape, texture, occlusion and garment continuity.
pending: New clothing01 pair, its retained AI sources and its measured registration are not yet available for final independent review.
